text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Interior Minister Ivan Penic announces the swapping of Croatian hard-back passports for soft-back ones in 1988, to meet European standards.
- The text of the Croat-Yugoslav agreement on border crossings may be finalised by the beginning of July. The two sides have agreed on the establishment of 13 border crossings.

- The Croatian social-liberals have lost in popularity since Vlado Gotovac became their leader. Former leader Drazen Budisa was supported by 21.9 percent of voters at the 1992 presidential elections, while Gotovac captured only 17.6 percent in the recent presidential elections.
- Parliament agrees to introduce new penal code articles covering money laundering, drug abuse and organised crime.

- The president of the parliament's undercommittee for relations with the European Parliament Zarko Domljan announces the introduction of changes to the 1995 law on taking over abandoned Serb property, during discussions with the European Parliament delegation led by Doris Pack.
- HSLS rogue member Dorica Nikolic says she would not listen to Vlado Gotovac and step down from the post of Zagreb's deputy mayor.
- Varteks, the Varazdin-based textiles producer gets an extension of its Levi's jeans production license for another five years.

- Government officials in charge of trade are announcing a "clean-up" operation that will cut down the number of shops per capita. The current European standard is one shop per 2,500 citizens, while in Croatia the figure stands at one shop per 64 citizens.
- I wish for all those who are not liberals to leave the party, says HSLS leader Vlado Gotovac in an interview.
- The Zadar Gold and Silver Exhibiton is reopened to visitors after seven years.
